tools.name: viz.render
tools.description: Renders a data-bound visualization spec from inline rows (or a datasetRef); explicit chartType+encodings or recommender-driven suggest mode. Returns a compiled Vega-Lite spec (ECharts opt-in) with a synthesized a11y description and a specRef for pipeline reuse.

tools.name: artifact.certify
tools.description: Certifies a Forge NormalizedVizSpec IR, optionally with the chart's DATA. Returns a per-pillar tri-state summary (a11yEquivalence, determinism, contrast, accuracy) that disaggregates what was actually checked, plus — on the cartesian path only — a folded conformance verdict (light theme). Read-only: reads the IR and the operand, never rebuilds or re-recommends. The 8 ECharts-primary types return coverage:'uncertified'/conformant:null — a distinct verdict, not a failure, and NOT a statement that nothing was checked: contrast has carried a real verdict for them since s141, and as of s172 DETERMINISM and ACCURACY do too whenever the caller supplies the optional `data` operand (the same data branch viz.render takes; exactly one branch, matching the mark trait). With it, certify re-emits the ECharts option twice and its contentHash equals viz.render's for the SAME (spec, data) pair, and it evaluates a per-type accuracy set (OODS-V154..V159); without it those two pillars stay 'unchecked' and notes[] names the missing operand. `data` on a cartesian spec is a structured error — dead input, not a silent no-op. Read accuracy:'pass' precisely: none of the rules OFFERED for that chart type positively detected its distortion, with accuracySummary.rulesEvaluated reporting how many actually ran; it is not a claim that the chart is accurate. a11y-equivalence remains 'unchecked' for these 8 — the equivalence engine has no per-rule not-applicable state, so that verdict migration is deferred to a warn-first rollout. IF YOUR CLIENT CACHES THIS TEXT (s173 m01): tool EXECUTION is read fresh from the built server on every call, so a Forge update reaches your results immediately — but this description and the input schema are what your connector advertised AT CONNECT TIME, so after a Forge release you are reading the old contract until you RECONNECT.

tools.name: dashboard.render
tools.description: Renders a composed metric-overview dashboard (KPI row + trend + breakdown + optional geo) from a declarative DashboardSpec; composes per-panel viz specs in-process with deterministic layout, KPI compute, and cross-filtering. Returns the resolved layout + per-panel specs + a synthesized a11y block and a specRef for pipeline reuse.
